_note: v2 hook overrides for le Sentier du Ciel Changeant (ST_ciel, S16_park), a showery spring-to-harvest meadow path of turf-roofed cottages; distinct from the Observatoire & météo (B32_ciel). Every hook describes what is actually painted (nothing is written in the paintings): Monsieur Verbe the striped mime acts out each verb; the hand mirror marks the one reflexive verb (s'épanouir).

fr_pleuvoir_verb.hook: A little gray cloud hangs over Monsieur Verbe and it RAINS on him: PLOP, PLOP on his umbrella (pleuh-VWAHR).
fr_pleuvoir_verb.why: PLOP of the rain → pleuvoir = to rain. Impersonal: only the il form exists (il pleut, il a plu, il pleuvra), so the card shows il forms only and no imperative. GOLD beret = irregular (il pleut).

fr_planter_verb.hook: Kneeling with his trowel, Monsieur Verbe PLANTS a young sapling (plahn-TAY).
fr_planter_verb.why: Plant → planter = to plant (nous plantons des tomates au printemps); also to drive in (a stake). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_couler_verb.hook: By the stream Monsieur Verbe watches the COOL water FLOW past as his paper boat goes down (koo-LAY).
fr_couler_verb.why: COOL water → couler = to flow (la rivière coule vers la mer); also to sink (le bateau coule). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_bruler_verb.hook: Ouch! Monsieur Verbe snatches his hand back from the piping-hot pie: like a crème BRÛLÉE fresh from the oven, it BURNS (brew-LAY).
fr_bruler_verb.why: Crème brûlée = burnt cream → brûler = to burn, to be burning hot (attention, le four brûle !). Painted as a hot dish only: no flames. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_luire_verb.hook: In the dark hollow under the hedge the black cat's eyes GLEAM like two little LURES as Monsieur Verbe peers in (LWEER).
fr_luire_verb.why: LURE gleaming in the dark → luire = to shine, gleam (les yeux du chat luisent dans le noir). GOLD beret = irregular (il luit, ils luisent; past participle lui).

fr_briller_verb.hook: In his sunglasses Monsieur Verbe holds up a gleaming wedge of BRIE and cheers YAY – BRIE-YAY, the cheese SHINES in the sun (bree-YAY).
fr_briller_verb.why: Brilliant → briller = to shine (le soleil brille). RED beret = regular -er. Oct30 1b: BRILLIANT was a cognate and the sun is outside the box; a shining Brie wedge was crop-edited into his hand.

fr_ensoleiller_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe flings open the shutters and the SOLEIL (sun) floods the cottage with light (ahn-soh-lay-YAY).
fr_ensoleiller_verb.why: En + soleil (sun) → ensoleiller = to fill with sunshine, to brighten up (ce sourire ensoleille ma journée). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_rallumer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe pulls the chain and the old street lamp's LUMIÈRE (light) comes back on: he RE-LIGHTS it (rah-lew-MAY).
fr_rallumer_verb.why: Re + allumer (to light, from lumière) → rallumer = to relight, switch back on (il rallume la lampe). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_eclaircir_verb.hook: On tiptoe Monsieur Verbe sponges the gray cloud away and the sky turns CLEAR and blue (ay-klehr-SEER).
fr_eclaircir_verb.why: CLEAR → éclaircir = to brighten, to clear (he clears the sky himself, so it is plain éclaircir: no mirror; the sky clearing on its own is le ciel s'éclaircit). GREEN beret = regular -ir (nous éclaircissons).

fr_polir_verb.hook: Sitting on his crate, Monsieur Verbe POLISHES the silver teapot until it sparkles (poh-LEER).
fr_polir_verb.why: Polish → polir = to polish (il polit les vieilles cuillères en argent). GREEN beret = regular -ir (nous polissons).

fr_dorer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe dips his brush in a pot of gold paint: everything he touches turns D'OR, golden (doh-RAY).
fr_dorer_verb.why: D'or (of gold) → dorer = to gild, to make golden; in the kitchen faire dorer = to brown (faites dorer les oignons). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_cultiver_verb.hook: With his hoe Monsieur Verbe CULTIVATES neat rows of young lettuces (kewl-tee-VAY).
fr_cultiver_verb.why: Cultivate → cultiver = to cultivate, to grow (ils cultivent des légumes). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_epanouir_verb.hook: Beside the rose bush in full bloom, Monsieur Verbe smiles into his hand mirror: he BLOSSOMS too, opening up like the roses, as happy as a PANSY in the sun (ay-pah-NWEER).
fr_epanouir_verb.why: S'épanouir = to bloom, to blossom (les roses s'épanouissent au soleil); used reflexively, so he holds the hand mirror and takes être (elles se sont épanouies). GREEN beret = regular -ir (nous nous épanouissons).

fr_exasperer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe throws both hands in the air: his lettuces keep getting nibbled and it EXASPERATES him (ehg-zahs-pay-RAY).
fr_exasperer_verb.why: Exasperate → exaspérer = to exasperate (ses retards m'exaspèrent). RED beret = regular -er. (j'exaspère, nous exaspérons).

fr_cherir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe hugs his little CHERRY tree, little hearts floating up: he CHERISHES it (shay-REER).
fr_cherir_verb.why: CHERRY / cherish → chérir = to cherish (elle chérit ses souvenirs d'enfance). GREEN beret = regular -ir (nous chérissons).

fr_fleurir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe gapes as the flower box FLOURISHES, bursting into FLEURS (flowers) (fluh-REER).
fr_fleurir_verb.why: Fleur (flower), flourish → fleurir = to flower, to bloom (les cerisiers fleurissent au printemps). GREEN beret = regular -ir (nous fleurissons).

fr_tacher_verb_2.hook: Oops! Monsieur Verbe stares at the coffee spill on his white apron: a brown STAIN shaped like a mous-TACHE (tah-SHAY).
fr_tacher_verb_2.why: Mous-TACHE → tacher = to stain (le café a taché ma chemise); une tache = a stain. Not to be confused with tâcher (with ^) = to try. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_mouiller_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe stands dripping in the sprinkler's spray: he is WET through, MOIST from beret to boots (moo-YAY).
fr_mouiller_verb.why: MOIST → mouiller = to wet, to make wet (la pluie mouille mes cheveux). RED beret = regular -er. (je mouille, nous mouillons).

fr_planer_verb.hook: Arms spread like the wings of a glider PLANE, Monsieur Verbe copies the eagle as it GLIDES overhead (plah-NAY).
fr_planer_verb.why: PLANE (glider) → planer = to glide, to hover (l'aigle plane au-dessus de la vallée). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_feuilleter_verb.hook: On his hay bale Monsieur Verbe LEAFS THROUGH his big book, and real autumn FEUILLES (leaves) flutter out of its pages (fuh-yuh-TAY).
fr_feuilleter_verb.why: Feuille (leaf, page) → feuilleter = to leaf through (elle feuillette un magazine). RED beret = regular -er. (je feuillette, nous feuilletons).

fr_couver_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe tucks a tiny knitted blanket over the hen as she COVERS her eggs: she is BROODING them (koo-VAY).
fr_couver_verb.why: COVER → couver = to brood, sit on eggs (la poule couve ses œufs); also to coddle. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_piloter_verb.hook: Oars in hand, Monsieur Verbe the captain PILOTS his little boat down the swollen river (pih-loh-TAY).
fr_piloter_verb.why: Pilot → piloter = to pilot, to fly or drive (il pilote un petit avion). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_inonder_verb.hook: Knee-deep in his vegetable patch among the ducks, Monsieur Verbe sees the river has INUNDATED his garden (ee-nohn-DAY).
fr_inonder_verb.why: Inundate → inonder = to flood (la rivière a inondé les champs). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_aerer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe shakes out the patchwork quilt to let the fresh AIR through it: he AIRS it (ah-ay-RAY).
fr_aerer_verb.why: Air, aerate → aérer = to air (ouvre la fenêtre pour aérer la chambre). RED beret = regular -er. (j'aère, nous aérons).

fr_deborder_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe gapes as the rain barrel fills right up and the water spills over its BORDER, the rim: it OVERFLOWS (day-bor-DAY).
fr_deborder_verb.why: Dé + bord (edge, BORDER) → déborder = to overflow (la rivière déborde après la pluie). RED beret = regular -er.
